column1: abasement§The general's public abasement—stripped of rank and paraded through the capital in chains—was recorded in every chronicle of the war.§这位将军当众**受辱**：军衔被剥夺，戴着镣铐押过都城，此事被每一部战争编年史记录下来。§ab-（向下）+ base（低的，同 basement 地下室）→ 压到低处
abate§The storm abated only near dawn, and the exhausted crew finally came up on deck to repair the torn sails.§风暴直到快天亮才**减弱**，筋疲力尽的船员这才上到甲板去修补撕裂的帆。§a-（去掉）+ bat（打，同 battle 战斗）→ 打下去

abbreviate§Headline writers abbreviate almost every long title, because a name that runs past the column edge simply will not fit the page.§标题编辑几乎会**缩写**所有长标题，因为一个跑出栏宽的名字根本排不进版面。§ab-（向）+ brev（短，同 brief 简短）

aberration§The unusually warm January was an aberration, not evidence of a new climate: the next four winters returned to normal.§异常温暖的那个一月只是一次**反常现象**，并非气候变化的证据——之后四个冬天都恢复了常态。§ab-（离开）+ err（走错，同 error 错误）→ 偏离轨道

abhor§She abhors any argument that dresses up cruelty as necessity, and she will walk out of a meeting rather than sit through one.§她**憎恶**任何把残酷粉饰成必要之举的论调，宁可退场也不愿听完。§ab-（离开）+ horr（发抖，同 horror 恐怖）→ 抖着躲开
abhorrence§His abhorrence of flattery was so complete that a single compliment could end a friendship of twenty years.§他对奉承的**痛恨**如此彻底，一句恭维就足以断送二十年的交情。§

abound§Errors abound in the first printing: whole paragraphs are repeated, and three chapters carry the wrong numbers entirely.§初版里错误**比比皆是**：整段整段地重复，还有三章的编号完全排错。§ab-（充分）+ und（波浪，同 abundant 丰富的）→ 像波浪一样涌来
abridge§The editors abridged the memoir by nearly half, cutting every passage in which the author settled old scores.§编辑把这部回忆录**删节**了将近一半，凡是作者算旧账的段落一律删掉。§a-（向）+ bridge ← brev（短，同 brief）→ 弄短
abridgment§The abridgment sold ten times better than the original, though scholars complained it removed exactly the passages that mattered.§这个**删节本**比原著多卖十倍，尽管学者抱怨它删掉的恰恰是最要紧的段落。§

abruptness§The abruptness of his departure startled everyone: he closed his laptop mid-sentence and left without a word of explanation.§他离开之**突然**让所有人吃了一惊——话说到一半就合上电脑，一句解释都没有。§ab-（离开）+ rupt（断裂，同 interrupt 打断）→ 突然断开
absolutist§The absolutist held that a monarch answers to God alone, and that any limit placed on his will is itself a crime.§这位**专制主义者**认为君主只对上帝负责，任何对其意志的限制本身就是罪行。§

absolve§The inquiry absolved the pilot of all blame, concluding that the instruments had failed long before he touched the controls.§调查**免除**了飞行员的一切责任，认定仪表在他碰到操纵杆之前很久就已失灵。§ab-（离开）+ solv（解开，同 solve 解决）→ 把责任解开

abstain§Two members abstained rather than vote against a colleague, and their silence decided the outcome as surely as any ballot.§两名成员选择**弃权**而不愿投票反对同事，他们的沉默像选票一样决定了结果。§abs-（离开）+ tain（拿住，同 contain 容纳）→ 手不伸过去
abstemious§An abstemious man all his life, he took neither wine nor second helpings, and outlived every friend at the table.§他一生**节制**，既不饮酒也从不添第二碗，比同桌的每一位朋友都活得久。§abs-（离开）+ tem（酒）→ 离酒远些
abstinence§Total abstinence from sugar for six weeks changed how food tasted to her, and she never went back.§六周完全**戒糖**改变了她对食物的味觉，从此再没回头。§

abstraction§The lecture disappeared into abstraction: an hour of definitions without one example a student could actually picture.§这堂课陷进了**抽象**——整整一小时都是定义，没有一个学生能想象得出的例子。§abs-（离开）+ tract（拉，同 attract 吸引）→ 从具体事物里抽出来
abstruse§The proof is so abstruse that even specialists in the field need a week and two commentaries to follow it.§这个证明**深奥**到连本领域的专家也要花一周、配两本注解才跟得上。§abs-（离开）+ trus（推，同 intrude 闯入）→ 推到远处藏起来
absurdity§The absurdity of the rule became obvious the day it required a fire crew to file paperwork before entering a burning building.§这条规定的**荒谬**在那天暴露无遗：它要求消防队进入着火建筑前先填表。§

accentuate§Black frames accentuate the pallor of the faces in these portraits, which is exactly the effect the photographer wanted.§黑色画框**凸显**了这些肖像中面孔的苍白，而这正是摄影师想要的效果。§ac-（加强）+ cent（唱，同 chant 吟诵）→ 加重音
acceptance§Her acceptance of the post surprised the department, since she had spent two years arguing the job should not exist.§她**接受**这个职位让全系吃惊，毕竟她花了两年论证这个岗位根本不该存在。§
accidental§The discovery was entirely accidental: a technician left a plate uncovered overnight and found the mold growing by morning.§这项发现完全是**偶然的**——一名技术员夜里忘了盖培养皿，早上就看到霉菌长了出来。§

acclaim§Critics acclaimed the debut so loudly that the publisher reprinted it three times before the author had finished her second book.§评论界对这部处女作**赞誉**之高，出版社在作者写完第二本书前就加印了三次。§ac-（向）+ claim（喊，同 exclaim 惊呼）→ 朝着人喊好
acclamation§The motion passed by acclamation—no one asked for a count, and the applause served as the vote itself.§这项动议以**欢呼**方式通过：没有人要求计票，掌声本身就是投票。§

accommodate§The old hall accommodates four hundred people comfortably, but the organizers sold seven hundred tickets and had to add a screen outside.§这座老礼堂宽松地**容纳**四百人，但主办方卖了七百张票，只好在外面加了一块屏幕。§ac-（向）+ com-（一起）+ mod（尺寸，同 mode 方式）→ 调到合适
accomplishment§Finishing the bridge in one season was an accomplishment no engineer on the crew had thought physically possible.§一个季度内建成这座桥是一项**成就**，队里没有哪个工程师原本认为它做得到。§
accost§A stranger accosted him outside the station, insisting they had met before and refusing to let go of his sleeve.§一个陌生人在车站外**搭讪**他，一口咬定两人见过，还抓着他的袖子不放。§ac-（靠近）+ cost（肋侧，同 coast 海岸）→ 贴到身边来
accusation§The accusation collapsed within a day: the witness had been three hundred miles away, and the receipts proved it.§这项**指控**一天之内就垮了——证人当时在三百英里外，收据可以为证。§ac-（向）+ caus（理由，同 cause 原因）→ 把事由算到某人头上

acquiesce§Rather than argue through another long evening, he acquiesced, and the plan he privately despised went forward unchanged.§为了不再争论一整晚，他**默许**了，那个他私下鄙夷的方案原封不动地推进下去。§ac-（向）+ quiesc（安静，同 quiet 安静）→ 安静下来不反对
acquiescent§Her acquiescent manner fooled the committee, which mistook a strategic silence for genuine agreement and moved on.§她**顺从**的姿态骗过了委员会，他们把一种策略性的沉默错当成真心赞同就翻篇了。§

acquisitive§An acquisitive collector, he bought faster than he could catalogue, and whole crates sat unopened in the basement for years.§这位收藏家**贪得无厌**，买的速度快过编目的速度，整箱整箱的东西在地下室搁了多年没开封。§ac-（向）+ quisit（寻求，同 require 需要）→ 一味往手里搜罗
acrid§Acrid smoke from the burning insulation drove everyone out of the building long before the alarm finally sounded.§绝缘层燃烧产生的**辛辣刺鼻**浓烟，早在警报最终响起前就把所有人赶出了大楼。§acr（尖锐，同 acid 酸）
acrimony§The negotiation ended in such acrimony that the two sides refused to sit at the same table for the next three years.§谈判在极度的**刻毒**中收场，此后三年两方都拒绝坐到同一张桌子旁。§acr（尖锐，同 acute 尖锐的）

acronym§NASA is an acronym, not a name: each letter stands for a word, and the agency's founders chose it for exactly that reason.§NASA 是一个**首字母缩略词**而非名字，每个字母代表一个单词，创始人正是看中这一点。§acro（顶端，同 acrobat 杂技演员）+ onym（名字，同 synonym 同义词）→ 取每词头一个字母
acumen§Her business acumen showed early: at nineteen she spotted the flaw in a contract that three lawyers had approved.§她的商业**敏锐**很早就显露出来——十九岁时就看出一份三位律师都批过的合同里的漏洞。§acu（尖，同 acute 敏锐的）→ 眼光尖

adamant§The landlord was adamant that the rent would rise, and no appeal to the tenants' twenty-year tenancy moved him at all.§房东**态度坚决**，租金非涨不可，租客住了二十年这一点丝毫打动不了他。§a-（不）+ dam（驯服，同 diamond 金刚石）→ 驯不服的硬东西
adaptable§Crows are unusually adaptable birds: they nest in traffic lights, open packaging, and learn a new city faster than most people do.§乌鸦是**适应力**极强的鸟：在红绿灯里筑巢，会拆包装，熟悉一座新城市比多数人还快。§
adept§She is adept at reading a room, and can tell within a minute which of two people actually makes the decisions.§她**擅长**察言观色，一分钟内就能判断出两个人里究竟谁说了算。§ad-（向）+ ept（拿到，同 apt 恰当的）→ 上手就拿得住
ad-lib§The lead actor ad-libbed two full minutes when the set collapsed, and the audience never realized anything had gone wrong.§布景倒塌时主演**即兴发挥**了整整两分钟，观众始终没发觉出了岔子。§

administer§A single nurse administers medication to forty patients on the night shift, which is why the hospital's error rate keeps rising.§夜班时一名护士要给四十位病人**给药**，这正是医院差错率不断上升的原因。§ad-（向）+ minister（仆人）→ 服务、料理
administrator§The new administrator cut three layers of approval, and a request that once took six weeks now clears in two days.§新任**管理者**砍掉了三层审批，过去要六周的申请如今两天就能办完。§
admonition§His father's admonition—never sign what you have not read—came back to him the moment the lawyer produced the contract.§父亲的**告诫**「没读过的东西绝不签字」，在律师拿出合同的一刻回到他脑中。§ad-（向）+ mon（提醒，同 monitor 监视器）
adorn§Gold leaf adorns every column in the hall, an extravagance that took four years and bankrupted the family that ordered it.§金箔**装饰**着大厅的每一根柱子，这份奢华耗时四年，也让订制它的家族破了产。§ad-（向）+ orn（装饰，同 ornament 装饰品）
adroit§An adroit negotiator, she conceded the point everyone was watching and quietly kept the three clauses that actually mattered.§作为一名**老练**的谈判者，她让出了众目睽睽的那一条，悄悄保住了真正要紧的三款。§
adulation§The adulation that followed his first film unnerved him: strangers quoted his lines back at him before he could order coffee.§第一部电影后铺天盖地的**吹捧**让他不安——他还没点上咖啡，陌生人就开始向他背诵台词。§
adulatory§The adulatory review reads like a press release, praising every choice and questioning none of them.§这篇**谄媚的**评论读起来像新闻稿，对每个选择都赞不绝口，一个也不质疑。§
advancement§Advancement at the firm depends less on results than on who happens to notice them, which is why she asked for a transfer.§这家公司的**晋升**与其说看结果，不如说看谁碰巧注意到了结果，所以她申请了调岗。§
advantageous§The treaty proved advantageous only to the side that drafted it, and the other signatories spent a decade trying to renegotiate.§这份条约只对起草方**有利**，其余签署国花了十年试图重新谈判。§

adversary§He treated every colleague as a potential adversary, and within a year no one would tell him anything worth knowing.§他把每个同事都当成潜在的**对手**，一年之内就没人愿意告诉他任何有价值的事。§ad-（朝）+ vers（转，同 reverse 倒转）→ 转过身来对着你

adversity§Adversity revealed what prosperity had hidden: the company had no plan, no reserves, and no one willing to make a decision.§**逆境**暴露了顺境掩盖的一切——公司没有计划、没有储备，也没有人肯做决定。§ad-（朝）+ vers（转）→ 事情转过来跟你作对
aerate§Gardeners aerate compacted soil each spring, because roots suffocate in ground that water and air can no longer pass through.§园丁每年春天给板结的土壤**松土通气**，因为在水和空气都过不去的地里根会窒息。§aer（空气，同 aerial 空中的）
aesthetic§Her objection was purely aesthetic: the building worked perfectly well, she said, but it made the whole street uglier.§她的反对纯属**审美**上的——她说这栋楼功能完全没问题，只是让整条街变丑了。§
affability§His affability disarmed the room; within ten minutes people who had come to complain were telling him about their children.§他的**和蔼**化解了满屋的火气，十分钟内那些本来是来投诉的人开始跟他讲自己的孩子。§
affable§The most affable person at the table was also the only one who remembered every name after a single introduction.§桌上最**和蔼可亲**的那位，也是唯一一个只听一遍介绍就记住所有名字的人。§af-（向）+ fa（说，同 fable 寓言）→ 好说话

affiliation§His affiliation with the institute is honorary, so he attends the dinners but has no vote and draws no salary.§他与该研究所的**从属关系**只是名誉性的，所以他出席晚宴，但没有投票权，也不领薪水。§af-（向）+ fili（儿子，同 filial 子女的）→ 收为子弟
affliction§Insomnia was the affliction that shaped his whole career: he wrote four novels in hours no one else was awake.§失眠是塑造了他整个事业的**折磨**——四部小说都写于旁人皆睡的时辰。§af-（向）+ flict（打击，同 conflict 冲突）
affluence§The town's sudden affluence came from a single factory, and when it closed the shops emptied within eighteen months.§这座小镇突如其来的**富裕**全靠一家工厂，工厂一关，商铺十八个月内就空了。§af-（向）+ flu（流，同 fluid 流体）→ 财富流进来
affordable§Nothing near the campus is affordable on a student stipend, so most first-years commute forty minutes each way.§校园附近没有一处房子是学生津贴**负担得起**的，所以多数新生单程通勤四十分钟。§
agent§The agent takes fifteen percent, and for that she reads every contract, argues every clause, and answers the phone at midnight.§这位**代理人**抽成百分之十五，作为回报，她审每份合同、争每个条款、半夜也接电话。§ag（做，同 act 行动）→ 替人办事的
aggrandize§Every renovation was designed to aggrandize the owner rather than improve the house, which is why the kitchen still leaks.§每一次翻修都是为了**抬高**主人的身价而非改善房子，所以厨房到现在还漏水。§ag-（向）+ grand（大）→ 弄大

aggregation§What looks like one organism is really an aggregation of thousands of separate cells that cooperate only when food runs short.§看着像一个生物体的东西，其实是数千个独立细胞的**聚合**，只有食物短缺时它们才协作。§ag-（向）+ greg（群，同 gregarious 群居的）→ 聚成一群
agile§Goats are astonishingly agile on rock: they cross a face in seconds that would take a trained climber an hour.§山羊在岩壁上**敏捷**得惊人——受过训练的攀登者要一小时的岩面，它们几秒就过去了。§ag（动，同 act 行动）→ 动得快
agitate§Union organizers agitated for a shorter week for eleven years before a single company agreed to try it.§工会组织者为缩短工时**鼓动奔走**了十一年，才有一家公司愿意试行。§ag（动）+ -itate（反复）→ 不停地搅动
agitation§His agitation was obvious to everyone: he checked the same empty inbox nine times in a quarter of an hour.§他的**焦躁**所有人都看得出来——一刻钟里他查了九次同一个空邮箱。§
agnostic§An agnostic refuses both answers: he holds that the question cannot be settled by evidence, and declines to guess.§**不可知论者**拒绝两种答案，他认为这个问题无法由证据裁决，也不愿去猜。§a-（不）+ gnos（知道，同 diagnose 诊断）
agreeable§The terms were agreeable to everyone but the one person who had to carry them out, and nobody asked her.§这些条件对所有人都**可以接受**，除了必须执行它们的那个人——而没人问过她。§
alacrity§She accepted the assignment with an alacrity that surprised her manager, who had prepared three arguments to talk her into it.§她**爽快**得让经理意外地接下了这项任务，而经理本已准备好三套说辞来劝她。§

allege§Prosecutors allege that the funds moved through four shell companies, though so far they have produced records for only two.§检方**指控**资金流经四家空壳公司，不过迄今只拿出了其中两家的记录。§al-（向）+ leg（说／法律，同 legal 法律的）→ 当众说出主张
alleviate§Nothing alleviated the pain until the third medication, and by then she had missed an entire semester of school.§直到第三种药才**缓解**了疼痛，那时她已经缺了整整一个学期的课。§al-（向）+ lev（轻，同 elevate 抬起）→ 把重担减轻
